note: pxPerUnit: art pixels per base unit at the default detail (RES 2): one art pixel = one world pixel, so a sprite's k is 1 / pxPerUnit. THE SCALE OF THE GAME (the owner, 2026-11-16): the grid of the sprite sheet ref/pip.png is the game's, one of its art pixels (about 2.86 picture pixels) is one game pixel, for every sprite, prop and tile alike. Pip stands 49 game pixels tall and is shown 1:1 (k .5: not halved, unlike Space Mouse's Pip); the sheet itself is about 380 x 213 game pixels, a 384 x 216 screen. The level picture ref/levelinspiration.png is a zoomed-out overview: one game screen covers about half its width and half its height.

character.note: Pip is 49 tall standing (ref/pip.png on the game grid), drawn and shown 1:1

styleParagraph: 16-bit SNES-style pixel art for a side-view platformer about a mouse astronaut in a cat-run space shipyard. A dark one-pixel outline round every character and prop. Bright, saturated, cheerful colours with two or three shades per material, light from the upper left, crisp hard pixel clusters, no gradients, no blur, no anti-aliasing. Pip: an orange mouse with big pink ears in a round glass space helmet, a white spacesuit with grey boots and gloves, a red-and-silver air tank on his back, a long red scarf flying behind him and a thin orange tail; he stands about 49 pixels tall.
